study_identification_part.si4_title: Normative modelling of molecular-based functional circuits captures clinical heterogeneity transdiagnostically in psychiatric patients

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The paper clearly states its objective to integrate REACT with normative modeling to capture individual-level deviations from health and link these to symptoms across diagnostic groups. It explains the purpose of applying normative modeling (individual-level deviations, translational utility, biomarker development). These satisfy both criteria (stated objectives and purpose of normative modeling).
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "We used REACT to create functional networks ... and generated normative models of these networks to capture functional connectivity deviations in patients with schizophrenia, bipolar disorder (BPD), and ADHD. ... linking constellations of symptoms through to underlying neurobiology transdiagnostically. This work provides impetus for developing novel biomarkers ... at the individual level"

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: NEW model built on healthy CamCAN and UCLA cohorts. Eligibility/inclusion–exclusion criteria for both healthy datasets are described in the supplement. Image quality and data completeness standards are specified (fMRIPrep QC, FD threshold, visual inspection). Final sample sizes for train/test partitions are reported; however, detailed counts of exclusions and explicit reasons per subject are not enumerated, so the reporting is incomplete.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: CamCAN eligibility criteria ... "no signs of diminished cognitive health ... no MRI safety contraindications"; UCLA healthy group criteria and exclusions ... "Participants in the healthy group [N = 130] were excluded if they had lifetime diagnoses of a psychiatric disorder ..."; Imaging QC ... "Participants with head motion exceeding 0.5mm framewise displacement were excluded ... quality control images and metrics were visually inspected ... participants additionally excluded for significant dropout ..."; Train/test sizes ... "resulting in CamCAN = 346/150 and UCLA = 78/33 train/test subdivisions"

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: The normative models include age and sex as fixed effects and model multi-site data by using site as a random effect within a hierarchical Bayesian regression framework, directly addressing key covariates and site effects.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: "... using the age and sex of participants to build a predictive model ... Specifically, we used site (UCLA, Cambridge) as a random effect as well as age and sex as fixed effects"

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: Data sources for the reference cohorts are explicitly stated: CamCAN healthy ageing dataset and UCLA OpenNeuro ds000030 phenomics dataset, with repository links and citation to the original publication.
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "Firstly, the healthy ageing CamCAN dataset (obtained from the CamCAN repository ...) ... Secondly, the UCLA phenomics dataset (ref. 120, available from https://openneuro.org/datasets/ds000030/versions/1.0.0)"

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: The study uses existing datasets (SECONDARY data), so per guidance this item is not applicable.

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: Preprocessing is described with software (fMRIPrep 20.2.5, ANTs, MCFLIRT, ICA-AROMA), steps (skull stripping, motion correction, co-registration, slice timing, smoothing, denoising, WM/CSF regression, high-pass filtering, MNI normalisation), and explicit QC criteria (FD > 0.5 mm exclusion, visual QC, exclusions for dropout/registration failures).
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: "FMRIPrep (version 20.2.5) was used ... motion using MCFLIRT ... boundary-based registration ... slice-time corrected, smoothed ... ICA-AROMA ... WM and CSF signals regressed ... high-pass filtered ... normalised to MNI ... Participants with head motion exceeding 0.5mm framewise displacement were excluded ... All fMRIPrep quality control images and metrics were visually inspected ... participants additionally excluded for significant dropout ... or repeated registration failures"

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: The study uses a 70/30 train–test split ensuring models are evaluated on held-out healthy subjects not used for fitting within the iteration.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "Normative models were trained on 70% ... and tested on the remaining 30% ..."; "... utilising a 70/30 train test split ... resulting in CamCAN = 346/150 and UCLA = 78/33 train/test subdivisions"

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: No independent external healthy dataset beyond CamCAN and UCLA was used for validating the normative models; evaluation was performed on held-out subsets from the same datasets.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "Normative models were trained on 70% ... and tested on the remaining 30% ..."

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: The approach is described in detail: hierarchical Bayesian regression implemented with PCNtoolkit (v0.27), site as random effect, age and sex as fixed effects, one model per ROI and receptor system, and software libraries specified (PCNtoolkit, sklearn).
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: "models using the PCNtoolkit (version 0.27) ... hierarchical Bayesian regression (HBR) ... used site ... as a random effect as well as age and sex as fixed effects ... A separate HBR model was estimated for each ROI and each receptor system ... train_test_split (sklearn)"

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: Model performance is reported as explained variance (EV) on held-out test data, with EV distributions across ROIs and networks shown (SI-Fig. 4), and the analysis restricted to ROIs with positive EV.
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "These trained models explained a moderate amount of variance (EV) ... This EV varied substantially ... (SI-Fig. 4). Herein, all analyses utilise only regions that had positive EV ..."
